description: No sabemos mucho, pero estamos dispuestos a saberlo todo
summary: Our project was focussed in creating a Space mission design game, so we developed a videogame that consists of space missions to the International Space Station, the Moon and Mars. The real challenge of this is to build your own rocket depending on what the mission requires, analyzing what items you need to carry like food and taking into account the weather conditions so the rocket can be launched correctly, all this to now all the things that have to be done before and when launching a rocket into the space
details: It is an interactive space mission simulation and decision-making video game, the main purpose is to guide the user through critical stages of a space flight like selecting a mission destination, Space Station, Moon, or Mars. Choosing a launch site, designing rocket, managing food rations for the crew and checking real weather conditions, all of this to make a successful launch. The game runs on a main loop managed by the Pygame library, handling keyboard inputs, mouse clicks, page-turning animations, and final victory - defeat animations. It evaluates the player's choices by accumulating structural damage or errors to determine whether the rocket launches successfully, sustains damage, or explodes. The main purpose of this is to function as an educational and entertaining tool that merges strategic decision-making with real aerospace concepts and technical engineering guidelines. It provides immersive visual interactivity, adapts to various screen resolutions, and allows players to consult technical rules at any time with the manual. We try to provide an engaging interactive experience where players learn about space mission planning, rocket engineering, logistics and data-driven launch weather considerations. The tools that we use were Python, Photoshop for graphics, the game loop, fonts, and UI along with standard Python libraries like `json`, `os`, `random`, `sys`, `threading`, `urllib.parse`, and Claude for making the code for the game. For data information ASA POWER API (`[https://power.larc.nasa.gov](https://power.larc.nasa.gov)`) for retrieving real meteorological data. An `assets` folder structure containing control room background images, rocket parts, weather icons, animations, and parameter positions stored in JSON files.
